name: Tarazed
description: A bright giant of type K3 II 121 parsecs away, 91.8 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 186791: radius 91.81 +2.19/-2.12 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 7.056 +/- 0.08 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 186791: mass 3.51 +/- 0.23 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 186791: effective temperature 4098 +/- 56 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 186791: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 8.26 +/- 0.17 mas, inverted

text.card: A bright giant of type K3 II, 121 parsecs away: 91.8 times the Sun's width and 2,146 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 7.056 milliarcseconds, which gives 91.81 solar radii and 4,098 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 186791: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4302054339959905920 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
